Caption: Table of Contents for Chapters 1 and 2.
Summary: This section of the table of contents outlines the structure of the first two chapters. Chapter 1 introduces high-temperature materials and superalloys, their applications in gas turbines, and methods for material selection. Chapter 2 delves into the physical metallurgy of nickel and its alloys, covering phases, defects, strengthening mechanisms, and creep behavior.

Caption: Table 1.1. Evolution of the features of large land-based industrial gas turbines [5]
Summary: This table documents the advancement of large land-based industrial gas turbines from 1967 to 1998, showing significant increases in performance metrics. Over three decades, turbine inlet temperatures rose from 900°C to 1425°C, pressure ratios doubled, power ratings more than quadrupled, and combined cycle efficiency improved from 43% to 58%.

Summary: This table details the specific superalloys and coatings used for vanes and blades in the hot sections of various industrial gas turbine models from manufacturers ABB, GE, Siemens, and Westinghouse/Mitsubishi as of 1997. Summary: This table shows calculated crack lengths at different stages of fatigue life for turbine disc alloys under various stress ranges. It lists the required non-destructive inspection limit (aNDI), crack lengths at one-third (3300 cycles) and two-thirds (6700 cycles) of life, and the critical crack length for fast fracture (acrit) at 10,000 cycles.

Caption: Table 4.5. Data for the inspectability of the Udimet 720 superalloy for various grain sizes, in the powder and cast-and-wrought conditions [56]
Note: ª Hole 1 corresponds to a diameter of 0.40 mm.
Summary: The table compares the ultrasonic inspectability of Udimet 720 based on its manufacturing process and grain size. Powder metallurgy forms, particularly those with smaller grain sizes (e.g., 3 µm), show significantly lower noise levels, indicating better inspectability. In contrast, the conventional cast-and-wrought form has a much higher noise level. Increasing grain size within powder metallurgy materials also degrades inspectability.
